answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound escrow before it may vote on a task or claim its reward. The protocol caps each account’s influence and releases the stake only after a challenge window, when peers can submit evidence of duplicate control; proven Sybils forfeit it. Splitting one owner across a marble, raven, and anchor account therefore does not create free influence: every extra identity ties up capital and risks losing it, making a mass attack costly.
